questions.question: What does a solution set contain?
options: Only the variables that appear in the equation.
All values or rules that satisfy the equation or system.

questions.question: Why is one correct solution not always enough to describe the solution set?
options: A solution set cannot contain numbers.
A solution set is always empty.
There may be other solutions that also satisfy the equation or system.
One solution is enough only for nonlinear equations, under all circumstances whatsoever.

questions.question: What do equivalent systems have in common?
options: The same number of symbols in each row.

questions.question: How are free variables usually recorded in a solution set?
options: By deleting all solutions except one.
By forcing the free variables to be zero.
By moving them outside the system.

questions.question: Can a solution set be empty?
options: Yes, if no value satisfies the equation or system.
Yes, but only for homogeneous systems.
No, every equation has at least one solution.
No, the empty set is not a set.

questions.question: What is the solution set of $x+2=3$ over $\mathbb R$?
What is the solution set of $x^2=1$ over $\mathbb R$?
Which pair belongs to the solution set of $x+y=10$?
Which parameterization describes all solutions of $x+y=10$?
What is the solution set of $0x=5$ over $\mathbb R$?
Why can $x=10-t$, $y=t$ be better than listing examples for $x+y=10$?
options: It describes all solutions at once.
It changes the equation into a contradiction.

questions.question: What mistake is made by saying “the solution set is $x=1$” instead of $\{1\}$?
options: It gives a condition rather than explicitly naming the set of solutions.
It incorrectly says $1$ is not a solution.
It claims there are two solutions.
It turns a real equation into a vector equation, for every possible choice of input.

questions.question: If two systems have different equations but the same solution set, what should they be called?
Which system has solution set $\{(1,1)\}$?
For $x=2t$, $y=1-t$, what equation is satisfied for every $t$?
Which equation has all real numbers as its solution set?
Why must the domain be specified when giving a solution set?
options: Solution sets are not sets unless the domain is finite.
The allowed values can change which solutions are included.
All domains give exactly the same solution set.
The equation itself disappears without a domain.

questions.question: An inconsistent system has no tuple satisfying all equations. Which set is its solution set?
options: An inconsistent system has empty solution set.
An inconsistent system has all vectors as solutions.
An inconsistent system has exactly the zero solution.
Inconsistency means the solution set is not allowed to be written.

questions.question: Over $\mathbb R$, what is the solution set of $x^2+1=0$?
Which parameterization gives the same solution set as $x+y+z=0$?
